lesson.title: Authorisation and urgency
lesson.summary: Apply prior binding authorisation, the urgent request deadline and immediate refusal consequences.

prerequisites.reason: The authority evaluates necessity and strict temporal, geographic and personal limits.

blocks: Each use requires **prior authorisation** by a judicial authority or an independent administrative authority whose decision is binding in the Member State of use, following a reasoned request and national detailed rules.

The competent authority needs objective evidence or clear indications that use is necessary and proportionate to a listed objective. Permission from a supplier or an operational colleague is not this binding authorisation.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(3), first and second subparagraphs

blocks: In a duly justified situation of urgency, use may commence without authorisation if authorisation is requested **without undue delay, at the latest within 24 hours**.
Twenty-four hours is the outside limit, not a normal waiting period. Record why urgency is justified and why the request is prompt. This rule concerns the request; it does not promise approval.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(3), first and second subparagraphs

blocks: If authorisation is rejected, use must stop with immediate effect. All data, results and outputs of that use must be immediately discarded and deleted.

Fictional Northbridge case: the authority refuses an urgent search request. Continuing while appealing or keeping outputs for possible future identification contradicts the specified immediate consequences.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(3), first and second subparagraphs

blocks: The authorising authority must keep time, geography and personal scope strictly necessary and consider the paragraph 2 harm/rights factors. A broad request cannot bypass these limits through urgency.
Maintain the request, evidence, decision and compliance record. An urgent request submitted promptly remains only a request until decided; the separate no-adverse-decision rule is taught in R05.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(3), first and second subparagraphs

questions.prompt: An operational manager approves a scan, but there is no decision from the competent judicial or independent binding administrative authority. What is missing?

options.blocks: The competent judicial or independent binding administrative decision

questions.prompt: A duly justified urgent use starts now. What is the request timing rule?

options.blocks: Wait at least 24 hours before requesting
options.reason: The statute requires promptness, not a waiting period.

options.blocks: Request only when the operation has finished
options.reason: That could breach both timing requirements.

options.blocks: Without undue delay, and no later than 24 hours
options.reason: Both the promptness requirement and outside limit apply.
